description: Male rats given the brain-penetrant microtubule stabilizer epothilone B took on average 69 seconds longer to lose the righting reflex under 4 percent isoflurane than vehicle controls, a Cohen’s d of 1.9, not explained by tolerance.
limitations: Behavioral latency in rats. The authors say the result is predicted by quantum microtubule models, but it does not by itself test quantum effects.

sources.quote: EpoB-treated rats took an average of 69 seconds longer to become unconscious as measured by latency to LORR.
